To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) hashtags can be used as a source of affective information, and (ii) affective information can be used to rank music recommendations.

(1) the affective information contained in hashtags is a valuable resource for ranking music recommendations, and (2) the ranking strategies that incorporate the affective information are able to capture a user’s context-specific music preferences well.
(1) hashtags can be used as context information to improve music recommendation and (2) affective hashtags can be used for capturing context-specific user preferences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How do users’ affective states influence their music choices?
the question how affective hashtags can be utilized to provide personalized music recommendations and how this can improve over existing methods.
the problem of how to incorporate context-specific affective information in a music recommendation setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ranking strategies that combine affective information and hashtag information are the most promising approaches to recommend music in the context of a specific mood.
a combination of affective and hashtag-based contextual information is most effective in the task of ranking music recommendations.
the latent representations of the users, tracks, and hashtags are complementary to the affective information, and thus, should be used jointly to rank music recommendations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
affective hashtags are a valuable resource for music recommendations.
affective hashtags can be used to capture context-specific preferences of users.

the latent representations learned for hashtags, users and tracks allow for capturing the general musical preferences of a user well, whereas the affective information contained in hashtags allows for capturing the context-specific preferences of a user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hashtags can serve as a proxy for capturing the emotional state of users, which in turn can be used for recommending music.

affective hashtags are a useful resource for music recommendation and that a combination of affective hashtags with latent feature representations of hashtags, users and tracks leads to a more accurate ranking of music recommendations than relying on either one of these resources alone.
the use of affective hashtags is a valuable source for capturing context information in the field of music recommendations.
